items.title: Why universities are rethinking written exams in the age of AI
items.originalSummary: As generative AI tools become widespread, several universities are piloting oral defenses, in-class essays and project-based portfolios to verify what students have actually learned.
items.learningSummary: Educational institutions worldwide are implementing significant changes to their assessment methods as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly prevalent. Rather than relying solely on traditional written examinations, numerous universities are now experimenting with alternative evaluation approaches. These innovative methods include oral defenses, in-class essay writing under supervised conditions, and project-based portfolios that demonstrate practical competencies. The primary objective of these reforms is to ensure academic integrity and accurately measure students' genuine understanding. Educators recognise that conventional testing formats can no longer reliably distinguish between original student work and AI-generated content. This shift represents a fundamental transformation in how academic institutions validate learning outcomes and maintain rigorous standards in an era of rapidly advancing technology.

readingQuestions.question: According to the passage, what alternative assessment methods are universities implementing?
readingQuestions.answer: Universities are implementing oral defenses, in-class essays, and project-based portfolios as alternative assessment methods.

readingQuestions.question: What can be inferred about the limitations of traditional written examinations in contemporary education?
readingQuestions.answer: It can be inferred that traditional written examinations are increasingly unreliable for verifying authentic student learning because they cannot effectively distinguish between human-generated and AI-generated responses.

readingQuestions.question: In the context of the passage, what does the phrase 'validate learning outcomes' most likely mean?
readingQuestions.answer: It most likely means confirming that students have genuinely acquired knowledge and skills, rather than simply producing outputs that may have been generated by artificial intelligence tools.

Do you think this is a positive or negative development for education? Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
items.listeningText: The landscape of higher education is undergoing a significant transformation as institutions grapple with the implications of artificial intelligence on academic assessment. Traditional written examinations, long considered the gold standard for evaluating student performance, now face scrutiny regarding their effectiveness in the digital age. Universities across the globe are responding by introducing diverse assessment strategies that better capture authentic learning. Oral defenses allow examiners to probe students' understanding in real-time, while project-based portfolios showcase practical application of knowledge over extended periods. These approaches not only reduce opportunities for academic dishonesty but also better prepare graduates for professional environments where problem-solving and communication skills are paramount. The transition reflects a broader recognition that assessment methods must evolve alongside technological advancements.

items.title: Why universities are rethinking written exams in the age of AI
items.originalSummary: As generative AI tools become widespread, several universities are piloting oral defenses, in-class essays and project-based portfolios to verify what students have actually learned.
items.learningSummary: Universities around the world are experimenting with new assessment formats as the use of generative AI tools spreads on campus. Instead of relying solely on take-home essays, some institutions are introducing oral defenses, in-class writing tasks and project-based portfolios that are harder to outsource. Supporters argue these methods give a more reliable picture of a student's real ability, while critics warn that they can be time-consuming and stressful for both students and staff. Educators broadly agree that the goal is not to ban technology but to redesign tasks so that AI becomes a study aid rather than a shortcut.

readingQuestions.answer: Because the spread of generative AI tools makes traditional take-home essays harder to verify.

readingQuestions.answer: They can be time-consuming and add stress for both students and staff.

readingQuestions.answer: They hand over the writing work to AI rather than doing it themselves.

items.writingPrompt: Some people think universities should redesign assessments because of generative AI, while others believe traditional written exams remain the fairest test. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
items.listeningText: Universities are quietly rethinking how they assess their students. With generative AI now widely available, take-home essays no longer prove what a student really understands. As a response, several institutions are piloting oral defenses, timed in-class writing and small group projects. Supporters say these formats offer a more reliable view of student learning, especially when combined with regular feedback. Critics, however, point out that they take more time to mark and can feel stressful for those who are not confident speakers. Most educators agree on one thing: the aim is not to fight technology, but to redesign assessments so that AI supports learning instead of replacing it.
